Resistance is a lot like friction; they both act to oppose motion
The power rating describes the amount of heat a resistor can safely give off.
If the amount of heat exceeds the power rating, the resistor will
Resistors must be able to dissipate or give off some of the heat
Power ratings are determined by the size and type of resistor.
A physically large resistor has more surface exposed to the air,
allowing more heat to dissipate. This is an overlay page.
Carbon composition resistors typically come in five sizes and power ratings. The power rating is measured in watts.

The next characteristic is tolerance. Enter the discussion text here.
Tolerance is the amount of difference that is acceptable between the measured ohmic value and the indicated value. This is also known as the percent of error.
Tolerance is usually described in percent, such as 1%, 5%, 10%, etc. This is an overlay page.
For example, if a 2000 ohm resistor has tolerance of 10%, its actual value could be anywhere between 1800 and 2200 ohms. Enter the discussion text here.
If a 2000 ohm resistor has a tolerance of 1%, its actual value could be anywhere between 1980 and 2020 ohms. Enter the discussion text here.
Notice as the tolerance decreases, the amount of the difference decreases. Enter the discussion text here.
Most carbon based resistors have a 5% tolerance. Enter the discussion text here.
Carbon based resistors are used in circuits that only require the accuracy to be within 5%. This is an overlay page.
Precision resistors have a tolerance of 1% or less.
Precision resistors are used in circuits that require an accuracy to be within 1%. This is an overlay page.
A resistor's tolerance is identified by a color band or is printed
on the resistor. Enter the discussion text here.

The power resistor's tolerance is printed on the body. his is an overlay page.
The precision resistor's tolerance is indicated in a code. ter the discussion text here.

The color code uses colors to represent numbers.
Each color on the chart is equal to a number or percentage.
The tolerance and ohmic value of a resistor is determined from the color bands. Enter the discussion text here.
The first band represents the first number in the resistance value. Red represents a 2. This is an overlay page.
The second band represents the second number in the resistance value. Black represents a 0. This is an overlay page.
The third band is the multiplier or number of zeros to add to the value of the resistor. Red represents 2 zeros. This is an overlay page.
The fourth band is tolerance. The ohm value and tolerance of this resistor is 2000 ohms at 5%. Gold represents 5%. This is an overlay page.
You may find that the third band of some resistors is silver or gold. In these cases the band is a multiplier with a value less than one. Gold is 0.1 and silver is 0.01..
1 out of 1000 fail during 1000 hours of standard operation.
Only military resistors have five bands. The fifth band is the reliability band. It indicates the percentage of failures for a group of identical resistors during 1000 hours of standard operation.
